extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, agents, and practitioners handling CNIPA patent reexamination and invalidation cases (China-focused)
extracted.subtask_description: Compilation of 72 key CNIPA decision points summarizing standards and approaches for patent reexamination and invalidation (novelty, inventive step, evidence, claims, specification, designs, procedures, etc.) applicable to Chinese patent practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence and explanation for invalidation based on “breach of good faith”
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 11 of the Implementing Rules of the Patent Law targets patent application behaviors that violate the principle of good faith, which is different from defects in the patent technical solution itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If this clause is used as a reason for invalidation, the applicant shall bear the burden of providing sufficient evidence and, based on the submitted evidence, provide a specific explanation of the patent application behavior that violates the principle of good faith. (Case No. 4W117458)

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration and division of labor between patent examination and food safety supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining whether a patent in the food sector involves “harming the public interest” as stipulated in Article 5 of the Patent Law, normative documents such as laws, regulations, and national standards related to food safety supervision serve as an important reference, but patent and food-safety systems have different objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because R&D and patenting generally precede production/sales licensing, requiring that all raw materials for food invention patents must already be in approved food raw material/additive catalogs may inhibit innovation. (Case No. 4W118080)

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination approach for food additive-related issues in food invention patents
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is evidence that a substance’s safety in food is recognized and no evidence that its use endangers health, using it in food inventions does not necessarily harm public interest; exceeding permitted concentrations may not constitute harm if widely recognized as safe and no evidence of danger exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider industry recognition and lack of evidence of harm rather than strict inclusion in existing standards. (Case No. 4W118080)

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of whether drug standard documents constitute public disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality standards of registered drugs archived in specific units such as the Drug Administration or Drug Testing Institute are usually only accessible to specific personnel and generally do not constitute disclosure within the meaning of patent law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 4W116478)

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of the time of publication of drug instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a drug has multiple versions of inserts and sales orders don’t indicate specific versions, drug name and sales time on a sales order alone cannot prove release time of a specific version of drug inserts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 4W116478)

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of the authenticity and release time of sold products (public use)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a product of the same model is obtained from multiple consumers via trade-in on an e-commerce platform, with notarized acquisition and transaction snapshots and no signs of replacement, it can be determined the product was publicly sold on the date the snapshot was generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 5W135377 Lighting mechanism and hair removal device)

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of the disclosure time of measuring instrument products
rubrics_metrics.description: For metering instruments, if meter readings match purchase/payment records and appraisal shows no disassembly/repair, the meter has been in public use since first payment; first payment date can be presumed public date of the meter product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 5W135507 Gas Meter Signal Acquisition Device)

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence for the claim of “open exhibition”
rubrics_metrics.description: A user-uploaded photograph and user-edited exhibition information without upload time, especially if inconsistent with other booth information, is insufficient to prove that an item was publicly exhibited at an exhibition before the application date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 6W116747 Bicycle (Women’s))

rubrics_metrics.name: Public recognition of use in special management places
rubrics_metrics.description: Products installed near the entrance of a restricted-access location, observable by passersby, should be deemed publicly knowable and thus constitute disclosure, even if other areas are closed and managed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 6W124834 Sliding Safety Wall)

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of the specific structure of the product sold publicly before the application date
rubrics_metrics.description: If a specific model was publicly sold before the application date and multiple corroborating sources record its specific structure, then absent contrary evidence those records can prove the product structure even if their disclosure time is later than the application date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 5W135632 A hydraulic support platform machine for underground working faces)

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of the authenticity and publication time of communication technology standard proposals (Internet disclosure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authenticity and publication date of standard proposals can be judged by the authority of the standards organization's website, working methods, membership, and server purpose; ITU uploads typically have system-generated upload dates usable as publication dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In absence of contrary evidence, ITU upload dates should be recognized as publication dates. (Case No. 4W111978)

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of the public date of archived web pages on the Internet Archive
rubrics_metrics.description: When using Internet Archive archives as prior art evidence, publication date should be determined with the site's URL naming conventions and numeric timestamp fields which indicate crawl/archive time; image and page crawl times may differ, and numeric fields in image URLs can be considered the image’s archiving time absent contrary evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 4W116322/4W116768 Multi-function Purifier)

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding the principle of single comparison in novelty judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: If a prior art document discloses the code name of a commercial chemical product but not its performance parameters, and the product’s structure/composition can be uniquely determined, introducing measurement results from other evidence merely confirms parameters and does not violate single-comparison principle for novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 4W117946/4W117974 Conductive Adhesive)

rubrics_metrics.name: The role of cited documents when using patent documents as comparative documents
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent document cites a background document that meets Patent Examination Guidelines, the patent document’s description is deemed to contain relevant content of the cited document; related content in cited documents can be considered disclosed and within reasonable expectation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 1F554680 User equipment equipped with SDR capabilities)

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of whether “background features” in HCI are disclosed by prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: In human-computer interaction, background processing features should be considered together with front-end features; if prior art doesn't clearly document background processing, consider from perspective of a person skilled in the art whether background methods can be directly and unambiguously determined from input/output behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 4W117583 Apparatus, method, and computer-readable storage medium for manipulating user interface elements)

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid taking the information disclosed in the prior art literally
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding prior art should be from the perspective of a person skilled in the art and avoid mechanically taking technically illogical or meaningless information as part of the disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 4W117756 Method for manufacturing resin for optical materials)

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of the technical content of video evidence disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical content in video evidence should be based on what can be directly and unambiguously determined from the video; short duration, bad angles, or low clarity that prevent direct determination render the video insufficient to prove disclosure of technical features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 4W117730 Intelligent Adjustment Method for Electric Curtains and Electric Curtain Rails)

rubrics_metrics.name: Can a PCT application be considered a “conflicting application”?
rubrics_metrics.description: After entering the Chinese national phase, a PCT international application has the same legal effect as a patent application filed directly with CNIPA; if statutory requirements are met, such PCT national-phase applications can be used as conflicting applications for novelty evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 1F609940 MPM list construction method...)

rubrics_metrics.name: The role of “cited documents” in determining priority
rubrics_metrics.description: If cited documents in background meet Patent Examination Guidelines, their relevant content may be deemed recorded in the patent; if a skilled person can understand the technical field, problem, solution, and expected effect of the priority document via the priority plus its cited docs, and they match the later application, the later application can enjoy priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 4W117594 “Ruxolitinib Phosphate” Case)

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for claiming a “grace period for not losing novelty”
rubrics_metrics.description: To claim the 6-month novelty grace period, disclosure must have occurred within six months before application, applicant must submit statement to CNIPA within two months after learning of disclosure with supporting materials, the disclosed solution must be directly/indirectly derived from applicant/inventor, and disclosure was without applicant’s consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 5W135853 Integrated Bracket Floating Breakwater Bracket)

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of the novelty of monoclonal antibody inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: If improvements lie in selective reduction of specific residues and nomenclature doesn't reflect oxidation/reduction, mere same nomenclature in prior art is insufficient to show lack of novelty; absence of prior-art preparation method and significant physicochemical differences also undermine novelty attack.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 4W116893 Selective Reduction of Cysteine Residues in IL-17 Antibodies)

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple distinguishing features that work together should be considered as a whole (inventive step)
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining distinguishing features and technical problems solved, multiple technical features that jointly achieve a function should be considered together rather than separately; organic differences in component structures/functions that jointly produce effect should not be split when assessing inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 1F450934 A plastic pellet processing system and processing technology)

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of different application scenarios on inventive step judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: If a claim’s technical solution differs from the prior art’s application scenario such that component functions and connections differ and yield beneficial effects, the claim may have an inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 4W111293 A chatbot system)

rubrics_metrics.name: Common knowledge may evolve over time
rubrics_metrics.description: Common knowledge in a technical field can change; if common-knowledge evidence post-dates the comparative document, that content cannot automatically be treated as implicitly disclosed in the comparative document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 1F483654 An analytical method for functional ingredients in cosmetic raw materials)

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of the role of distinguishing features in reference documents (technological inspiration)
rubrics_metrics.description: When judging whether prior art provides technical inspiration, analyze whether the technical means disclosed in the reference play the same role or solve the same problems as the distinguishing features, from the skilled person’s perspective and considering the overall work process recorded in the reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 1F516906 Chip Heat Exchanger and Inverter Air Conditioner)

rubrics_metrics.name: Existing technologies in different application fields can provide combined inspiration
rubrics_metrics.description: In inventiveness assessment, re-determine the technical problem based on the closest prior art; prior art in similar or related fields that shows same technical means solving same problem can provide inspiration to combine with closest prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 4W116379 Adsorption-type self-moving device)

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of sequence of process steps on technological inspiration judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Order of process steps may be constrained by component structures; if prior art discloses substantially same steps in different order, consider whether component differences prevent reversing order—if so, prior art cannot be considered to provide inspiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 4W116776 A processing technology for a fake inner mold)

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of specification’s technical effect on the three-step method conclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: If the three-step approach indicates the prior art contains suggestion for combination, the invention is obvious; other technical effects described in the patent do not alter this if skilled persons can determine the effects from the combined prior art solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 4W116583 Electromechanical Rear Derailleur)

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of parameter characteristics in technological inspiration
rubrics_metrics.description: For claims with specific parameter features, if closest prior art has same components and similar parameters and provides guidance on parameter selection, and patent spec doesn't show the parameters yield significantly better effects, the parameters are routine choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 4W117515 Method for producing knot yarn and vortex nozzle)

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of technological inspiration of combination drug inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: For combination drug inventiveness, consider whether prior art provides expectation of successful replacement, differences between drug types/mechanisms, and whether mere general mention of combination is sufficient—general mention is insufficient to prove clear technical inspiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 1F409289 Combination Use of Nitroxanol...)

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of technical inspiration of medical inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: If prior art broadly lists many candidate indications without verification and pathogenesis/treatment mechanisms differ widely, skilled persons generally cannot obtain clear technical inspiration from such documents for different indications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 1F409289 Combination Use of Nitroxanol...)

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of combining different versions of communication standards in inventive step
rubrics_metrics.description: If distinguishing features are partially disclosed in documents from different versions of communication standards applicable to different scenarios solving different problems, such documents cannot be considered to provide inspiration for introducing the distinguishing features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 4W116433 Carrier Aggregation Feedback Method...)

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of supplementary experimental data (inventiveness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effects shown by supplementary experimental data must be obtainable from disclosures in the original application; if effects are measured under conditions clearly stated or concretely manifest effects described originally, they can serve as factual basis for inventive step evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 4W117821 “Fruquintinib Crystal Form” Case)

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of inventiveness of Traditional Chinese Medicine compositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Flexibility in adjusting ingredients/dosages doesn't mean arbitrary combination is allowable; medicinal compatibility principles based on syndrome differentiation must be adhered to, and if only conventional efficacy of individual ingredients is known without understanding position/function/structure and without guidance, the composition is likely non-obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 4W116478 A Chinese medicine composition for treating femoral head necrosis...)

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of inventiveness of crystalline forms of pharmaceutical compounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Polymorph identification is common; inventiveness generally recognized only when unexpected technical effects exist; conventional technical means to obtain crystal forms lower inventive-step expectations and technical means used are important factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 4W117821 “Fruquintinib Crystal Form” Case)

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of creativity for medical use inventions indicated by physiological indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: If refining pharmaceutical use by characterizing the administration subject via a physiological indicator that has clinical medication guidance value, the indicator can substantially impact scope of protection; determine technical problem and whether indicator connection to therapeutic effect is shown sufficiently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 4W117065 Use of Degarelix...)

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventiveness examination for applications involving computer-assisted medical technology
rubrics_metrics.description: If a computer-assisted medical solution is based on existing modeling tech and only incorporates typical medical simulation parameters without producing technical effects beyond existing simulations, it lacks inventiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 4W116678 Inspection Methods for Computer-Assisted Orthodontic Appliances)

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventiveness assessment of technical solutions for achieving HCI using AI technology
rubrics_metrics.description: For model training to simulate personalized behavior, focus on whether specific objects, scenarios, and training objectives substantially impact the technical solution. If prior art doesn't involve a modified model for such training and scenarios/data/training differ, prior art doesn't provide inspiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 1F399901 Virtual Robot Interaction Method...)

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of application scenarios in determining inventiveness of AI algorithm patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess inventiveness for AI algorithms applied to specific scenarios by considering scenario and model algorithm as a whole; if model differs in training data, input/output, model selection, etc., due to scenario differences and solves different technical problems, it can be inventive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 1F397311 Method and apparatus for processing images)

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of inventiveness for claims with parameter relationships in optical lenses
rubrics_metrics.description: For optical imaging systems designed with software, judge creativity by retracing design process; consider whether creative work determined initial structure and parameter constraints. Classify parameters into those with inevitable linkage and those without; linkage implications affect whether parameters can be fixed or change during optimization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 4W115749 Camera Optical Lens)

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for citing foreign patent documents in patent background art
rubrics_metrics.description: If a foreign patent document cited in background was published no later than the patent in question, its content can be used as basis for determining disclosure content of the patent application or right, even if application submitted before implementation of newer guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 4W117594 “Ruxolitinib Phosphate” Case)

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for level of detail in description for sufficiency of disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifications and embodiments should be as detailed as possible, but not every detail must be listed; if omitted technical details are achievable by skilled persons via common knowledge or conventional means and omission doesn’t preclude solving the technical problem, omission does not amount to insufficient disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 4W117305 Mayonnaise-like food)

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of whether a technical solution containing parameter features is sufficiently disclosed
rubrics_metrics.description: If the specification only states the parameter relationship to be satisfied but provides no technical means for implementing it and no theoretical rules, the solution cannot be implemented due to lack of technical means, causing insufficient disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 4W116759 A negative electrode sheet, secondary battery, and electrical device)

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding of “Created Words” in claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms in claims are generally understood with meanings commonly used in the technical field. For made-up words without common meaning, interpret objectively based on claim limitations, description of the technical problem, and technical effects in the specification; patent examination files are references for scope understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 4W117583)

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding the scope of protection of process claims
rubrics_metrics.description: For method claims, if a skilled person can determine that a certain process step is implicitly defined by other steps through overall understanding of process flow and connections, then even if not in claim text it should be considered part of scope of protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 4W117474 Preparation of Acrylic Acid)

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent claims should state necessary technical features — role of essential technical features
rubrics_metrics.description: Essential technical features are indispensable for solving the invention's technical problem and their sum is sufficient to constitute the invention’s technical solution distinct from background art; requiring these in independent claims ensures the claim-defined solution can solve the claimed problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 4W117786 Composition containing amlodipine and bisoprolol)

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims should be based on the description — support determination based on intended technical problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a claim is supported by the description should be determined based on the technical problem the invention intends to solve, using background, objectives, technical problem/beneficial effects, and specific implementation content, not on the technical problem actually solved in inventive step analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 1F678174 Preparation Method of Hydroxymethylfurfural)

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding the “generalization of claims” in support judgments
rubrics_metrics.description: When judging support, clarify the technical problem the patent intends to solve and then assess whether claim generalization departs from the technical means and problem as disclosed in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 5W135482 A power tool)

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreting “amendment timing” and claim text in consolidated hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: When two invalidation requests are heard together and the patentee submits amendment text timely for one request but not the other, the amendment text that meets timing should be used for the combined hearing to maintain consistency of examination text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 5W132976/5W133604 A rotating opening and closing base structure and air purifier)

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment requirements for claim scope narrowing
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments must not add new technical content beyond original disclosure; narrowing claim scope is permitted but must be supported by the original application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General principle reflected across claim/amendment decisions. (Implied across claims-related cases)

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of added subject-matter when amending claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments are disallowed if they introduce technical content that a skilled person could not derive directly and unambiguously from the original disclosure; the support requirement is assessed in light of the technical problem and the original description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied in support and amendment cases (referenced in multiple case points).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary value of a unilaterally commissioned appraisal opinion in invalidation proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: If an appraisal opinion commissioned by one party contains obvious flaws—sample cleanliness, experimental conditions, accuracy of results, or standardization issues—the collegial panel will not recognize its evidentiary value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 4W115889 An electrode sheet and a lithium-ion battery containing the same)

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of witness testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Testimony of an interested witness generally cannot alone determine facts; however, if testimony is logically clear, without contradictions, and corroborated by other evidence, it can form a link in the chain of evidence and be probative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 5W132828 A CNC wire saw)

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine correspondence between sales page and product on shopping website
rubrics_metrics.description: If a shopping website assigns unique product codes to items, there is generally a strict correspondence between sales page and physical product identified by code unless evidence shows platform rules violated; burden of proof lies with party claiming mismatch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 5W132976/5W133604 A rotating opening and closing base structure and air purifier)

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding “perfecting the legal form of evidence” in invalidation proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary evidence that is identical to the principal facts in original evidence and serves to make form comply with statutory requirements or more authoritative is 'perfecting the legal form'; if supplementary evidence adds new facts it does not perfect form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 5W135315 A vehicle-mounted integrated camping box and camping box system)

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of the use of public “chain of evidence” (standard of proof)
rubrics_metrics.description: When one piece of evidence has limited probative value, consider whether multiple pieces corroborate each other to form a chain of evidence; with comprehensive consideration of industry practice, if petitioner meets burden and patentee fails to produce contrary evidence, the high probability standard may be met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case Nos. 4W116721, 4W116782, 4W116834, 4W117343 Hot-pressed high-strength components...)

rubrics_metrics.name: The review panel may reasonably change how evidence is used (procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: During review, the collegial panel may, based on file evidence used in substantive examination, appropriately adjust the way evidence is used including changing combination of evidence, changing closest prior art, or changing cited parts; this does not exceed reasonable expectations of requester and can enhance rationality/sufficiency of examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 1F478571 Semiconductor Wafer Surface Topography Measurement Device...)

rubrics_metrics.name: A request for invalidation may be made against a patent that was valid before abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patentee files a declaration of abandonment and rights terminate from issuance of the formalities acceptance notice, an applicant may still file for invalidation for the rights that were valid from application date to formalities acceptance notice date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 5W136585 Coil Devices and Components with Configurable Turns)

rubrics_metrics.name: The role of “expert opinions” in invalidation procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If an expert opinion is not used to prove case facts but instead evaluates facts (especially providing legal judgments), it can only be used as a reference for the panel and not as evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 4W115889 An electrode sheet and a lithium-ion battery containing the same)

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of amended text in consolidated trials of multiple invalidation requests
rubrics_metrics.description: In combined hearings, if the patent owner submits amendment text that meets timing for one request but not others, the timely amendment should be used as the text for the combined hearing to maintain consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 5W132976/5W133604 A rotating opening and closing base structure and air purifier)

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding the conflict of interest of an agency in invalidation procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant and patentee in same invalidation case may not entrust the same patent agency; if agency’s prior acceptance of matters causes or may cause damage to interests of the other party, agency shall not be allowed to act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 4W116237 Screw compressor with multi-layer coated rotor screw)

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative judgment of partial design (design examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: For partial design comparisons adopt 'overall observation and comprehensive assessment' starting with the part for which protection is sought (solid lines); 'overall' refers to the part not entire product; consider visual impact of differences/similarities and changes in position/proportion within overall product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 6W128122 The connection between the spray gun nozzle and the machine body (partial))

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of product type on validity of a design combination and method of judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Same or similar product categories are not necessary for a valid design combination; consider whether content used is an existing design feature that can be naturally distinguished, whether features have same/similar uses or precedents, and whether combination exceeds ordinary consumer cognition; if conditions met, combination can be valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 6W126786 Toy (Bubble Tank))

rubrics_metrics.name: Judgment on legal use of trademark rights by design patent holders
rubrics_metrics.description: If trademark text/design on patented packaging box is identical to patentee’s registered trademark and partially identical to applicant’s trademark, identical portion is overlapping marks and both may lawfully use them; lawful use for patentee’s approved goods category does not deny use for applicant’s category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 6W125581 Packaging Box (Extended Twist Drill))

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of scope of rights of prior trademarks with high reputation in rights conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining design conflict with prior trademark, goods category is not absolute limit; consider distinctiveness, reputation, relevance, and subjective bad faith; high-reputation trademarks may have scope extended to different/dissimilar categories to prevent weakening or exploitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 6W124730 Wine Box (Yuguihetianxia))

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of cases involving conflicts between design patents and copyrights
rubrics_metrics.description: When petitioner claims work was made into animated video and publicized and thus patentee had access, first examine relevance between work and video, relationship of copyright holder and publisher, similarity of static/dynamic images and timing; then determine whether release constitutes disclosure per platform mechanisms—if public before application date, patentee had access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. 6W127201 Milk Dragon Fan)

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding 'commercial utilization' of integrated circuit layout designs
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Commercial utilization' per Regulations on Protection of Integrated Circuit Layout Designs refers to importing, selling, or otherwise providing protected layout designs, integrated circuits, or items for commercial purposes; 'providing in other ways' is equivalent to import and sale and excludes promised sales not actually occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. JC0027 GLF71301)

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of originality in integrated circuit layout designs
rubrics_metrics.description: An exclusive right holder’s prior layout-design also counts as comparative layout-design; to qualify for exclusive protection a subsequent layout-design must be substantially different from prior design and difference must not be a generally recognized conventional design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Case No. JC0027 GLF71301)
